title: only1
statement: Write a program that displays a 1 character and nothing else.

title: onlyz
statement: Write a program that displays a z character and nothing else.

title: CountAlpha
statement: Return the number of alphabetic characters (a-z, A-Z) in s.

title: CheckNumber
statement: Return true if the string contains any digit.

title: RectPerimeter
statement: Return the perimeter of a w x h rectangle, or -1 if either is negative.

title: PrintIf
statement: Return "G\n" if len(str) >= 3 or str is empty, otherwise "Invalid Input\n".

title: HashCode
statement: For each char: (ASCII + len(dec)) % 127; if the result is unprintable (below 32, or 127) add 33. Return the new string.

title: FirstWord
statement: Return the first word of s followed by "\n". Words are delimited by spaces.

title: LastWord
statement: Return the last word of s followed by "\n".

args: this ... is sparta, then again, maybe not

title: Gcd
statement: Return the greatest common divisor of two uints; 0 if either is 0.

title: DigitLen
statement: Return how many times n can be divided by base until 0. base must be 2..36 else -1. Negative n: flip the sign.

title: Itoa
statement: Re-implement strconv.Itoa (handle the minus sign). No imports.

title: FromTo
statement: Return numbers from..to as two-digit values separated by ", ", ending in "\n". If either is <0 or >99 return "Invalid\n".

title: ThirdTimeIsACharm
statement: Return every third character of str followed by "\n" (just "\n" if there is none).

args: a b c d e f

title: WeAreUnique
statement: Count distinct characters that are in only one of the two strings. 0 if none; -1 if both empty.

title: ZipString
statement: Run-length encode: each group of identical neighbours becomes count+char.

title: FindPrevPrime
statement: Return the first prime <= nb, or 0 if none.

title: fprime
statement: Print the prime factors of a positive int, ascending, separated by '*', then a newline. Wrong arg count, invalid input, 0 or 1: print nothing. Only os.Args and printing runes (z01).

title: hiddenp
statement: Take s1 and s2. Print 1 if s1 is hidden in s2 (its chars appear in order, not necessarily adjacent), else 0, then a newline. Empty s1 is hidden. Wrong arg count: print nothing.

title: inter
statement: Print, without doubles, the chars that appear in both strings, in the order of the first, then a newline. Wrong arg count: print nothing.

title: union
statement: Print, without doubles, the chars that appear in either string, in command-line order, then a newline. Wrong arg count: print just a newline.

title: wdmatch
statement: If the first string can be written using chars of the second, in order, print the first string and a newline; otherwise print nothing. Wrong arg count: nothing.

title: FifthAndSkip
statement: Separate every five characters with a space and remove the sixth. Spaces inside the input are ignored. Fewer than 5 chars: "Invalid Input\n". Empty: "\n".

title: NotDecimal
statement: Take a float string and return it as an int string without the decimal point (multiply by 10^n). No decimal point or only a zero after it: return the number. Empty or not a number: return it unchanged.

title: RevConcatAlternate
statement: Takes two []int, returns a new slice of alternated values in reverse order. The longer slice's extra elements come first (reversed); if lengths are equal start with the first slice.

title: Slice
statement: Slice(a []string, nbrs ...int) []string: cut a from the first int to the second (or to the end if only one). Integers can be negative.

title: findpairs
statement: Take a quoted int array like "[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]" and a target. Print "Pairs with sum T: [[i j] ...]" (indices). Messages: "No pairs found.", "Invalid target sum.", "Invalid number: x", "Invalid input."

title: revwstr
statement: Print the words of the argument in reverse order, then a newline. Words are alphanumeric, separated by exactly one space. Wrong arg count: print nothing.

args: the time of contempt precedes that of indifference
tests.out: indifference of that precedes contempt of time the

title: rostring
statement: Rotate the string one word to the left (first word becomes last), words separated by one space. Wrong arg count: print a newline.

title: WordFlip
statement: Return the words in reverse order followed by "\n". Collapse multiple spaces and trim. Empty string: "Invalid Output".

title: ItoaBase
statement: Convert value to a string in base 2..16 using digits 0-9 then uppercase A-F. Negative values get a leading '-'.

title: options
statement: Args starting with '-' are options a-z; print them as 4 bytes (32 bits, bit0=a ... bit25=z) in groups of 8. No args or -h first in an arg prints "options: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz". Any invalid option: "Invalid Option".

title: piglatin
statement: Print the Pig Latin of the argument: word starting with a vowel (aeiou, any case) gets "ay"; otherwise move leading consonants to the end then add "ay". No vowels: "No vowels". Wrong arg count: print nothing.

title: romannumbers
statement: Convert the number argument (1-3999) to a roman numeral. Print its calculation, e.g. C+X+X+I+I+I (subtractive parts as (M-C)), then the numeral on the next line. Invalid number, 0 or 4000+: "ERROR: cannot convert to roman digit".

tests.out: ERROR: cannot convert to roman digit
ERROR: cannot convert to roman digit
ERROR: cannot convert to roman digit

title: brackets
statement: For each argument print OK if its (), [], {} are correctly bracketed, otherwise Error. Other chars are ignored; no brackets is OK. No arguments: print nothing.

title: rpncalc
statement: Evaluate the RPN expression in the single argument (+ - * / %) and print the result. Extra spaces are fine. Invalid expression or arg count != 1: print Error.

title: brainfuck
statement: Write a Brainfuck interpreter. Source is the first argument; 2048-byte array of zeros, pointer at the first byte. > < + - . [ ] ; any other char is a comment. No argument: print nothing.

title: grouping
statement: Replicate regex brackets: args are a pattern like "(a)" or "(e|n)" and a text. Print each match's containing word (punctuation stripped) as "N: word", in order, one line per match. Wrong arg count, invalid pattern, empty text or no match: print nothing.

args: I'm heavy, jumpsuit is on steady, Lighter when I'm lower, higher when I'm heavy
I currently have 4 windows opened up… and I don’t know why.
tests.out:
1: currently
2: currently
3: have
4: windows
5: opened
6: opened
7: and
8: don’t
9: know

args: He swore he just saw his sushi move.
